turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Um, thank you so much for seeing me. 

I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... well, my supervisor actually suggested I come in. I work in production, and I try really hard to do a good job, I promise. But I guess I have this bad habit of, um, leaving my station? Or like, I'll just pop up out of my chair during our shift meetings when we're supposed to stay put. 

I really don't mean to be disruptive! It's just... I sort of take off before I even really think about it. My supervisor said it's becoming a safety problem, which made me feel awful, because I really don't want to cause any trouble or make anyone mad. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to figure out how to be better at work.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they have a habit of leaving their station and popping out of their chair during meetings when they are supposed to stay put.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had this tendency to act impulsively or get up when you are supposed to stay seated since you were a child, or is this something that only started recently?
turns.patient_response:
Um, well... I guess it's not exactly new. I really hope that's okay to admit. Even way back in elementary school, I was kind of... well, I was the kid who couldn't really stay in my seat. 

I never meant to be a bother to anyone! I just... I would get too eager and accidentally talk over the teacher, or I'd get notes sent home to my parents because I'd blurt things out or end up wandering around the room when we were supposed to be working. I always tried really hard to be good, I promise, I just had so much energy and I'd sort of act before I realized what I was doing. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible student... did I answer your question okay?

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they could not stay in their seat and would wander around the room during elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient mentions getting notes sent home because they would blurt things out.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient admits to accidentally talking over the teacher, indicating interrupting or intruding.

turns.doctor_question: Beyond the restlessness and acting impulsively, do you find that you also struggle with things like sustaining your focus on tasks, losing important items, or frequently forgetting appointments or chores?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm any worse at that stuff than anyone else. I always try my best to pay attention, especially at work, because I really want to do a good job. 

I guess I might misplace my keys sometimes, but everyone does that, right? I really try to be responsible and stay on top of my chores and everything. I don't want you to think I'm, like, totally disorganized or careless. I really do put a lot of effort into keeping things together. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too confusing.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient denies struggling to sustain focus, stating they always try their best to pay attention.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly denies being disorganized, stating they put a lot of effort into keeping things together.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient denies clinically significant loss of items, stating they only misplace keys sometimes like everyone else.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient denies forgetting chores, stating they stay on top of their chores and responsibilities.
